newsitem.title: UK: Euro crude under pressure but holiday thins trade.
newsitem.headline: Euro crude under pressure but holiday thins trade.

text.p: A U.K. holiday thinned trade on European crude oil markets but those continental traders in the office on Monday said the tone remained weak following Friday's selloff.

IPE Brent crude closed some 30 cents down on Friday as late profit-takers sold heavily into the close. Dull refiner buyer interest amid poor profit margins and ample supplies of Brent, Russian and North Afrcan grades also put pressure on physical differentials.
By Monday afternoon, traders assessed October Brent paper at $20.35/$20.40, slightly down from Friday's IPE close of $20.41.
The October crude futures contact on NYMEX ACCESS on Monday last traded at $21.96, down three cents from Friday's close.

Dated Brent was assessed at 15-20 cents a barrel under September paper, down 10 cents from Friday's high point, following a trade as low as -20 cents late Friday between a U.K. major and a trading company for a September 7-9 cargo.
But some traders said the low price was the result of manipulation of dated Brent values to offset CFD positions. This week's CFDs were talked as low as September -25 cents late Friday.

Med traders noted that while simple refiner margins have improved by 50 cents a barrel from Tuesday to Friday, they are far from good. "We are still looking toward perhaps cutting runs if we do not see a bigger improvement. There is still no reason to increase our crude oil buying," said a trader at one of the Med's largest refiners.
Last week, a handful of European refiners cut runs which combined with heavy autumn refinery maintenance work threatens to dull crude buying interest even further.
